title: Switzerland, Austria and Germany: The Alps from Geneva to Munich in 15 Days
meta_title: Switzerland Austria Germany 15 Days: Zermatt to Munich
meta_description: 15-day Alps journey: Montreux, Zermatt and the Matterhorn, the Jungfraujoch, Lucerne and Rigi, Bern, Innsbruck, Königssee, Salzburg and Neuschwanstein.
tagline: The Matterhorn, the Top of Europe and the fairy-tale castle of Bavaria
facts: Montreux 2, Zermatt 2, Interlaken 2, Lucerne 2, Zurich 1, Innsbruck 2, Salzburg 1, Munich 2
Swiss Travel Pass for 9 days, then a rental car from Innsbruck
Active, with an easy Zurich day
intro: A mountain-lover's route through three countries. Lake Geneva and Glacier 3000, the Matterhorn from Zermatt, the Jungfraujoch glacier from Interlaken, Mount Rigi above Lucerne, and the old towns of Bern and Zurich, all by train on the Swiss Travel Pass. A rental car then takes you through the Tyrol to Innsbruck, Lake Königssee, Salzburg and Neuschwanstein Castle before Munich. We changed the original Austria days, which put Innsbruck, Swarovski and Hallstatt in one day: Hallstatt is about 3 hours from Innsbruck each way, not 1 hour 30 minutes, and Königssee is about 2 hours 15 minutes away. You now drive from Innsbruck to Königssee and sleep in Salzburg, and visit Neuschwanstein as a day out from Munich.

good_to_know.title: Two currencies
good_to_know.text: Switzerland uses Swiss francs (CHF); Austria and Germany use euros. Cards are accepted almost everywhere, including mountain restaurants. Swiss prices are much higher than in Austria and Germany.

good_to_know.title: Swiss Travel Pass
good_to_know.text: Covers trains, buses and lake boats in Switzerland, with discounts of 25 to 50% on most mountain railways such as the Gornergrat and the Jungfraujoch.

good_to_know.title: Altitude and weather
good_to_know.text: Above 3,000 m, a mild headache and breathlessness are normal. Go up in the morning: afternoon thunderstorms between about 14:00 and 17:00 can stop cable cars. Use SPF 50 sunscreen.

good_to_know.title: Driving in Austria and Germany
good_to_know.text: Indian licence holders need an International Driving Permit. Austrian motorways need a digital vignette bought before you drive; Germany has none. Traffic drives on the right.

good_to_know.title: Hotel deposit
good_to_know.text: Use a credit card for the deposit or pre-authorisation at check-in, never a forex or debit card. Forex cards cannot hold funds, many hotels refuse them, and a credit-card hold is released faster.

good_to_know.title: Cards and cash
good_to_know.text: On card machines, always choose to pay in Swiss francs or euros, never in INR. Carry about CHF 50 and EUR 50 in cash for small kiosks and toilets.

good_to_know.title: Pickpockets
good_to_know.text: Busy stations, trams and squares are pickpocket hotspots. Keep passports in the hotel safe, carry a copy, and wear your bag in front in crowds.

good_to_know.title: Plugs, water and meal times
good_to_know.text: Plugs are the two round-pin type C and F at 230 volts (Switzerland uses type J; a type C plug fits). Tap water is safe to drink. Lunch is about 12:00 to 14:00 and dinner from about 18:30.

best_time: June to September, when every mountain railway runs and the Alpine meadows flower. July evenings are light until about 21:30.
seasons: Green valleys, waterfalls in full flow and fewer crowds; some high passes and lifts open only from late May or June.
Warmest weather and every lift open; busiest and most expensive.
Clear autumn days and quieter trains; some lifts close for maintenance from late October.
Snow and Christmas markets; skiing in the mountains, short days in the cities.

faqs.q: Is there a version starting in Vienna?
faqs.a: Yes. Our second plan starts with three days in Vienna and Bratislava, then drives through Salzburg, Zell am See with the Grossglockner road and the Kaprun spa, and Innsbruck to Munich.
Only from Innsbruck. We can replace the car with a driver or with trains and a day tour to Neuschwanstein.
Yes. We have arranged surprise cakes on the Jungfraujoch and tandem paragliding over Zell am See for graduations and anniversaries.

faqs.q: Can this itinerary be changed for our dates and pace?
faqs.a: Yes. Every Blue Diamond Voyage itinerary is a starting point. We change the number of nights, the hotels, the pace and the activities to suit your family, and send you a personalised quote.

faqs.q: Do you look after vegetarian and Jain food?
faqs.a: Yes. We send your dietary brief to every hotel and guide before you travel, and suggest pure-vegetarian restaurants along the route. Jain meals without onion, garlic and root vegetables can be arranged in most places with notice.

dining_intro: Vegetarian food is easy to find in every city on this route; Jain meals take planning. We send your dietary brief to every hotel and tour, and list Indian and vegetarian restaurants near each hotel in your travel pack.
dining_avoid: Soups, sauces, risottos and even some vegetable dishes are often made with meat or fish stock, and many cheeses use animal rennet. Show the food card and ask before ordering.
food_card: Wir sind strenge Vegetarier. Kein Fleisch, kein Fisch, keine Meeresfrüchte, keine Eier. Keine Zwiebeln, kein Knoblauch, keine Kartoffeln, keine Karotten, kein Wurzelgemüse. Keine Fleisch- oder Fischbrühe. Danke.

Nous sommes végétariens stricts. Pas de viande, poisson, fruits de mer ni œufs. Pas d'oignon, d'ail, de pomme de terre, de carotte ni de légumes racines. Pas de bouillon de viande ou de poisson. Merci.
We are strict vegetarians (Jain). No meat, fish, seafood or eggs. No onion, garlic, potato, carrot or any root vegetables. No meat or fish stock. Thank you.
